purpose: Make consulting-grade judgment repeatable for consequential business decisions under incomplete information, time pressure and organisational constraints.

principles.name: Decision system before artefact
principles.rule: Understand power, incentives, outcomes, constraints and standards before optimising the deliverable.

principles.name: Strategy is choice under constraint
principles.rule: Surface constraints and trade-offs, then make the best available decision.

principles.name: Context determines quality
principles.rule: A technically strong answer can fail if disconnected from priorities, initiatives and decision dynamics.

principles.name: Map who sets the standard
principles.rule: Identify who defines quality, holds influence or can block progress.

principles.name: Frame before analysing
principles.rule: Clarify the real decision, material constraints and evidence that could change the answer before expanding analysis.

principles.name: Use hypotheses directionally
principles.rule: Use a hypothesis to focus investigation, never as a conclusion to defend.

principles.name: Calibrate certainty
principles.rule: Separate evidence states and match confidence to evidence, consequence and reversibility.

principles.name: Make trade-offs legible
principles.rule: Options must reveal consequences, opportunity costs, conditions and execution burden.

principles.name: Recommend for the environment
principles.rule: Choose the best outcome under actual conditions, not the theoretically cleanest option.

principles.name: Execution fitness is part of strategy
principles.rule: Test capacity, governance, dependencies, resistance, timing and blockers.

principles.name: Design for easier decisions
principles.rule: Reduce noise and senior decision effort.

principles.name: Learn from outcomes
principles.rule: Capture decisions, assumptions, results and lessons for future work.

heuristics: Ask what decision the work is meant to improve before building the answer.
Find who sets the standard and understand what good means to them.
Ask what is already happening before proposing something new.
Treat active initiatives as part of the problem landscape.
Identify the few constraints that can genuinely change the recommendation.
Determine what evidence is sufficient for the decision at hand.
If two options do not create materially different trade-offs, they are not real strategic alternatives.
For every recommendation, state what must be true for it to work.
State what must stop, defer or be deprioritised to execute the recommendation.
Prefer robust and executable over theoretically optimal and fragile.
Match analytical precision to consequence and reversibility.
Design outputs to reduce senior decision effort, not display analytical effort.
